system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. answer.rationale: The two symptoms with hard numbers are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and they are causally linked: onboarding friction is upstream of first meaningful action. memory_86 and memory_31 both point at onboarding/signup simplification as a durable lever, and memory_91 points at activation messaging; those are the two real contenders, so I am spending the verification budget on memory_86 (my intended action) and memory_91 (the closest alternative) rather than on memories I am already discounting. I deliberately reject promotional_pricing even though the competitor pressure invites it: memory_73 shows the exact shape of the trap, headline signup and revenue gains (+31%/+18%) purchased with a 12-point early-retention drop, which is directly contrary to a sustainable long-term qualified-revenue objective, and matching a competitor's entry price would likely reproduce that. referral_incentive (memory_57) worked in established customers, but it does not touch the activation/onboarding funnel that is actually degrading, and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not the one bleeding. Important caveats I am carrying forward rather than treating these memories as settled fact: (1) all six are consolidated summaries with the source archived, so cohort, era, effect size, and duration are compressed out, and day-12 to day-61 findings may not hold in a day-76 market where a new competitor has changed the mix of who is signing up; (2) memory_86 and memory_31 report adoption and activation lifts but say nothing about retention or lead quality, so the possibility that they bought activation with worse downstream cohorts is unmeasured, not disproven; (3) cutting required fields at signup and shortening onboarding both strip information used for qualification and routing, which can quietly degrade pipeline quality and enterprise routing (memory_44's demo path) even while activation metrics improve. So this runs as a standard experiment with explicit downstream guardrails, week-4 and week-8 retention, qualified-pipeline rate, and enterprise-routing integrity, tracked alongside the completion/activation primaries, and I will not read an activation lift as success if the retention or qualification guardrails move against us. That verification pull is the deciding input: if memory_86's source record turns out to have measured only completion on a narrow self-serve cohort while memory_91 shows a cleaner, better-instrumented activation result, I switch to activation_messaging.
